studio_binding_proposal.canonical_blob_tier: ArtifactStore (UUID-addressed, manifest per file, atomic write, hash-verified, GC). Loom blobs (<root>/data/workspaces/<ws>/assets/<tier>/<hash>) are the non-canonical second tier and become a migration target: new Studio/CKC bytes never go there.
studio_binding_proposal.why: ArtifactStore already has the invariants the spec demands (manifest = PRIM-ArtifactManifest, write-once, refuses content_hash != sha256(payload), read-time re-verification, layers, retention fields) and it is the tier CKC media rows already bind to via artifact_ref. Loom blobs have no manifest, no read verification, no GC, and a row-then-blob ordering with no compensation; their one advantage, HTTP Range, is a feature to port rather than a reason to keep a second tier. Choosing ArtifactStore meant porting only a READ path plus a streaming WRITE path, both now landed; choosing Loom would have meant rebuilding manifests, verification and GC from scratch.

read_path_contract.manifest_identity: PRIM-ArtifactManifest = artifact://.handshake/artifacts/<layer>/<uuid>/artifact.json; the placed-asset link's artifact_manifest_id is that ref (or the (layer, uuid) pair)
read_path_contract.resolve_bytes: GET /atelier/media-assets/{asset_id}/bytes -> 200 bytes with Content-Type (catalog MIME), Content-Length, ETag "sha256-<hex>", Cache-Control private,immutable, x-hsk-artifact-ref, x-hsk-content-sha256; 404 unknown asset or missing payload; 400 non-native artifact_ref; 500 any integrity mismatch (row vs manifest, manifest vs payload). Store-level equivalent: AtelierStore::read_media_asset_bytes. The link's resolved_content_hash is x-hsk-content-sha256; link state: resolved when it equals the stored resolved_content_hash, modified when it differs, missing on 404-unknown, unresolved before first call. unauthorized cannot be produced yet: no ResourceBroker in the base (WP-KERNEL-006/007); until then the route is actor-attributed (x-hsk-actor-id) but not authorization-enforced and the spec should say so explicitly instead of implying the state exists.
read_path_contract.streaming: Read is buffered today: the whole payload is hashed and verified before the first byte is sent, so a client never receives partial bytes on an integrity failure, but there is no HTTP Range support. VERIFIED: the Loom tier already implements Range (api/loom.rs get_asset_content, GAP-LM-009b) without verification; the ArtifactStore route verifies without Range. The proposed convergence keeps verification and adds Range by hashing once per artifact and caching the verdict (or verifying the served slice against a per-artifact chunk map), so video seeking works without giving up fail-closed reads. Write IS streaming and size-capped: POST /atelier/media-assets hashes and counts as it writes.

studio_binding_proposal.crash_consistency_rule: Order is blob -> verify -> catalog row (the Atelier pattern), never row -> blob (the Loom pattern). If the row write fails or dedups, the writer removes the blob it just wrote (compensation). Rows and their EventLedger event must commit in ONE SurrealDB transaction (the stage_artifacts.rs BEGIN/COMMIT pattern); the reference branch post-commit event writes (MT-056 F10) must not be ported as-is. VERIFIED GAP: a hard crash strictly between payload rename and row commit leaves an orphan L1 artifact that nothing reclaims - storage::retention::plan_ttl_artifact_gc scans ONLY ArtifactLayer::L3 and prunes only manifests carrying retention_ttl_days (pinned and TTL-less manifests are always spared), and atelier::filesystem_health is documented read-only (it never resyncs, deletes, repairs or creates media rows) and merely records an UntrackedOriginal finding. The mirror case, a catalog row whose payload is gone, surfaces as a 404 on the byte route and a MissingOriginal finding, and is likewise never auto-repaired. An orphan is never served and re-ingesting the same bytes dedups on content_hash, so this is a disk-usage and hygiene gap, not a correctness one.
studio_binding_proposal.size_limits_and_eviction: Ingest ceiling HANDSHAKE_MEDIA_INGEST_MAX_BYTES (default 4 GiB) enforced while streaming; the JSON/base64 Loom import is bounded by Axum 2 MiB plus the same decoded cap and is not a bulk path. VERIFIED eviction scope: plan_ttl_artifact_gc reads only <workspace>/.handshake/artifacts/L3, spares pinned manifests and every manifest with no retention_ttl_days, and deletes only past-TTL artifacts. Studio/CKC originals are written to L1 with retention_ttl_days=None, so they are never evicted by any current path - which is the desired posture for originals and matches the spec intent that media originals are excluded. Proposed: derived previews/proxies for Studio go to L3 WITH a TTL so they are the only evictable tier; originals stay L1 and TTL-less; and a future L1 sweeper must treat a live placed-asset link as a reference (it cannot simply delete unreferenced L1 payloads while documents hold links).
studio_binding_proposal.viewport: CKC's Atelier panel IS Studio's asset viewport: Studio opens it as the CKC module in the module rail (or a workbench pane) with a target ref (atelier://media/<asset_id>, atelier://collection/<id>, atelier://character/<id>) and gets back placed-asset picks through the typed drag payload / asset.place command. What it shows: character-scoped albums, media grid with real bytes via the byte route, tags/notes/ratings, Posekit/OpenPose, intake batches, search. Models drive it through the 128 stable atelier-ckc-* AccessKit ids (Argus list_widgets/click_widget/set_value/screenshot); MT-065 ports them verbatim and the report lists them.
spec_should_say: STU-ASSET-025 close: the artifact tier is storage::artifacts (ArtifactStore): UUID-addressed under <workspace>/.handshake/artifacts/<layer>/<uuid>/{payload,artifact.json}; manifest = PRIM-ArtifactManifest; write-once, hash-verified on write and read; GC; layers L1-L4; API = write_file_artifact / write_file_artifact_streaming / read_file_artifact / read_artifact_manifest / remove_file_artifact plus HTTP GET /atelier/media-assets/{id}/bytes and POST /atelier/media-assets; transactional relationship: blob before row, compensation on row failure, row+event in one SurrealDB transaction.
STU-ASSET-004: name Loom blobs as the existing violation and require consolidation onto the ArtifactStore (migration WP), not a retroactive ban.
STU-ASSET-005: artifact_manifest_id is the ArtifactStore manifest ref; resolved_content_hash is bare lowercase sha256 hex (the x-hsk-content-sha256 header).
STU-ASSET-007: state that `unauthorized` is producible only once WP-KERNEL-006/007 ship ResourceBroker; until then resolution is attributed, not authorized, and MUST NOT be reported as `missing`.
STU-ASSET-008: bulk binary MUST ingest through the streaming route with the ceiling; base64/JSON ingest is forbidden for Studio assets.

STU-ASSET-012..014: export-back = POST /atelier/media-assets (streamed) + catalog row + derivation edge; the edge record does not exist yet in CKC (no atelier derivation table) and MUST be added before export-back is claimed.

STU-ASSET-004 evidence: the port introduced NO third blob tier. Every filesystem write under src/atelier and the atelier API was checked; the two live writers are in validator_first_pass.rs and both exist at base 1d47363f, and the remaining three are inside #[cfg(test)] fixture modules. api/loom.rs now points bulk-binary callers at POST /atelier/media-assets and states it is not a bulk-binary path.

STU-ASSET-008/009: a SECOND verified byte route exists and is stricter, not weaker. GET /atelier/posekit/openpose-png/bytes?artifact_ref= resolves the manifest, requires a Posekit-generated L1 image/png, requires a rendered atelier_pose_sidecar row bound to the same ref, and requires that row to agree with the manifest on hash (via the canonical sha256_refs_match), size and MIME before reading; it then goes through the same read_file_artifact_with_manifest, so the payload is re-hashed exactly as on the media route. Sidecar missing = 404, sidecar-vs-manifest drift = 500. Studio inherits the same guarantee on Posekit exports.
declared_debt: Orphan L1 payload reclamation has no owner: retention GC is L3+TTL only, filesystem_health is report-only. Needs either an L1 sweeper that is link-aware or a write-ahead intent record so an interrupted ingest is resumable/rollback-able.
CKC has no derivation-edge table, so STU-ASSET-014 (source asset -> derived export edge) cannot be satisfied today; it must be added before export-back is claimed.
STU-ASSET-007 `unauthorized` is not producible: no ResourceBroker/Principal in the WP-KERNEL-012 base; resolution is actor-attributed, not authorization-enforced.

artifact_store.manifest: yes (PRIM-ArtifactManifest: mime, size, content_hash, classification, retention_ttl_days, pinned, source refs)
artifact_store.write: atomic temp -> fsync -> rename; refuses content_hash != sha256(payload); write-once
artifact_store.read_verification: yes - read_file_artifact re-hashes the payload against the manifest before serving

loom_blobs.write: write_file_atomic after the row is created (row -> blob, no compensation)
loom_blobs.read_verification: none - api/loom.rs get_asset_content resolves the path from the row content_hash and streams the file without re-hashing
loom_blobs.range_requests: YES (GAP-LM-009b, honors HTTP Range for long-video seeking)
